record.title: ZCode documents no default OS sandbox for its shared Agent adapter and a yolo default for non-interactive CLI prompts
record.summary: The ZCode v3.15.1 repository commit dated 2026-10-10 includes a Chinese NOTICE stating that its shared Agent execution adapter has no default operating-system sandbox, and that standalone CLI --prompt calls default to yolo when --mode is omitted. The pinned CLI source defines that fallback, and its permission service describes prompt-bypass rules and exceptions. These findings are scoped to the documented adapter and non-interactive CLI path; no packaged runtime was tested.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: ZCode's NOTICE says the shared Agent execution adapter does not provide a default operating-system sandbox and warns that workspace identity, Git worktrees, browser isolation and Node REPL context are not system-level isolation guarantees for all tools.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The current CLI run.ts source defines the default headless prompt mode as yolo and passes mode ?? DEFAULT_HEADLESS_PROMPT_MODE when invoking a non-interactive --prompt request without an explicit mode.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The permission service says yolo mode bypasses permission prompts for ordinary tool calls when plan mode is not enabled; separate checks retain user-interaction and always-ask handling, while NOTICE distinguishes other execution surfaces and host-controlled modes.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: No packaged ZCode v3.15.1 binary or operator deployment was inspected; the source files were pinned to the v3.15.1 repository commit, but deployment-added isolation and effective runtime behavior were not tested.

evidence_gaps.description: No packaged ZCode v3.15.1 binary or runtime environment was inspected, despite the source files being pinned to the release commit.
No runtime test confirmed the effective approval prompts or OS-level isolation of a packaged or deployed ZCode configuration.

brief.importance_rationale: If these documented defaults apply to the inspected ZCode CLI/shared-adapter revision, they materially affect isolation and approval assumptions for agent runs that can execute tools under the host account. Score 4 reflects an actionable harness-selection and deployment concern; the statement is scoped to documented modes and is not a claim that all ZCode surfaces share these defaults.
limitations: The no-default-sandbox statement is scoped by the NOTICE to the shared Agent execution adapter; it should not be generalized to every ZCode tool or operating mode.
The yolo default applies to standalone non-interactive CLI --prompt calls when --mode is omitted, not automatically to interactive TUI or every desktop, resumed, target or host-managed execution.
The permission service retains separate user-interaction, always-ask, disallowed-tool and plan-mode logic; 'yolo' is not evidence that all interactions bypass every control.
The inspected source files are pinned to commit aac4755666d09fdcd70272fcf063c077a639015f, identified as the v3.15.1 update. No runtime test or distributed binary inspection was performed.
The repository source does not establish whether an operator's deployment adds external OS sandboxing or other isolation.

The pinned CLI source defines that fallback, and its permission service describes prompt-bypass rules and exceptions. technical.claimed_result: The project documentation states there is no default OS sandbox for its shared Agent execution adapter and that non-interactive standalone CLI --prompt runs default to yolo without --mode.
technical.demonstrated_result: The current repository NOTICE and CLI source contain the scoped statements and code paths described. Runtime behavior in a pinned packaged build was not tested.
technical.mechanism: The CLI's non-interactive prompt path falls back to yolo when no prompt mode is supplied. The permission service's mode logic allows ordinary tool calls in yolo mode without permission prompts, while user-interaction and always-ask capabilities have separate checks. Independently, the repository NOTICE says the shared Agent execution adapter has no default OS sandbox.
technical.novelty: The material information is the repository's explicit, mode-scoped disclosure of sandbox and approval defaults; no novelty claim is made about the underlying permission architecture.
technical.regime: ZCode v3.15.1 commit aac4755666d09fdcd70272fcf063c077a639015f, dated 2026-10-10. Findings concern the shared Agent execution adapter and standalone CLI non-interactive --prompt path, not all ZCode execution surfaces.
technical.reproducibility: The NOTICE and both source files were bound to the same release commit SHA using path-specific GitHub commit history. Source paths are pinned; no packaged binary or runtime behavior was tested.
technical.strongest_baseline: No cross-project comparison is claimed. Within ZCode, NOTICE distinguishes the shared adapter and standalone CLI prompt path from interactive, desktop, resumed and host-controlled modes; build and plan modes have separate permission behavior.

brief.title: ZCode documents no default OS sandbox for its shared Agent adapter and a yolo default for non-interactive CLI prompts
brief.why_it_matters: Users selecting an agent harness need to know whether ordinary file, shell and network operations receive operating-system isolation and whether unattended CLI calls require explicit permission prompts. ZCode's own documentation and source expose materially different defaults by execution mode, so treating project-level approval as a uniform security boundary would be unsafe.
